public.terms.title: Terms and conditions
public.terms.intro: These terms describe the intended use of TeamBalance as an operational management platform for project-based agencies and consulting firms.
public.terms.section1.title: 1. Purpose of the service
public.terms.section1.paragraph1: TeamBalance is a software-as-a-service platform designed to centralize information about projects, tasks, availability, skills, seniority and operational workload. Its purpose is to support resource planning and assignment within an organization.
public.terms.section1.paragraph2: Any recommendations, projections and alerts shown by the platform are decision-support tools. Final validation of assignments, deadlines and employment decisions always remains the responsibility of the customer organization.
public.terms.section2.title: 2. Access, accounts and roles
public.terms.section2.paragraph1: Access is provided through personal accounts associated with an agency or organization. Each user must keep their credentials confidential and use the platform according to their assigned role.
public.terms.section2.paragraph2: Owner, Project Manager and Employee profiles may view and operate different information according to their permissions. The agency administrator must manage the creation, removal and access levels of their team based on necessity and minimum exposure.
public.terms.section3.title: 3. Responsible use and uploaded data
public.terms.section3.paragraph1: The customer organization is responsible for the accuracy, legitimacy and currency of the data entered into TeamBalance, including information about people, projects, tasks, availability and clients.
public.terms.section3.item1: Data whose processing is not authorized by the organization or applicable regulations must not be uploaded.
public.terms.section3.item2: The platform must not be used to infringe third-party rights, breach confidentiality or perform unlawful activities.
public.terms.section3.item3: People-management decisions must not rely solely on an automated recommendation.
public.terms.section4.title: 4. Plans, purchase and subscription
public.terms.section4.paragraph1: Published plans describe the billing period, functional scope and reference value of the subscription. Purchase is formalized through the specific TeamBalance flow and the commercial conditions in force at the time of the request.
public.terms.section4.paragraph2: Activation, renewal, suspension or cancellation of a subscription is linked to its contract status and the information recorded for the agency. Billing conditions, payment methods and validity will be clearly shown during checkout.
public.terms.section5.title: 5. Availability and product evolution
public.terms.section5.paragraph1: TeamBalance is designed to provide continuous and reliable access to operational information. However, maintenance, updates, incidents or infrastructure dependencies may temporarily affect availability.
public.terms.section5.paragraph2: The platform may evolve its features, interfaces and policies to improve security, performance or user experience. Relevant changes will be communicated through available account channels or in this public section.
public.terms.section6.title: 6. Intellectual property and confidentiality
public.terms.section6.paragraph1: The TeamBalance brand, interface, documentation, components and product logic belong to their respective owners or are used with proper authorization. A subscription grants a limited right to use the service for the subscribed period; it does not transfer intellectual-property rights.
public.terms.section6.paragraph2: Operational information entered by an agency remains under that organization’s responsibility. TeamBalance may process it only as necessary to provide, maintain, support and protect the service.
public.terms.section7.title: 7. Suspension and termination
public.terms.section7.paragraph1: Access may be preventively limited if there is a security risk, use contrary to these terms, harm to third parties or a substantiated operational need. Where reasonable, the measure will be communicated to the account administrator.
public.terms.section7.paragraph2: When the service relationship ends, the applicable retention, backup and deletion criteria will be applied according to the privacy policy, technical requirements and applicable obligations.
public.terms.notice: The current version of these terms remains available on this page. The specific conditions of each purchase supplement this general framework of use.
public.privacy.title: Privacy policy
public.privacy.intro: This policy explains what information TeamBalance may process, why it is used and what controls are considered to protect it.
public.privacy.section1.title: 1. Information that may be processed
public.privacy.section1.paragraph1: To provide the service, TeamBalance may process account and organization data such as name, email address, role, access data and operational preferences. It may also process information that each agency records to manage its projects, tasks, availability, skills, seniority, workload and clients.
public.privacy.section1.paragraph2: The platform is intended for operational information. Customer organizations should avoid entering sensitive personal data or information that is not necessary for planning and management purposes.
public.privacy.section2.title: 2. Processing purposes
public.privacy.section2.item1: Create and manage accounts, roles, sessions and subscriptions.
public.privacy.section2.item2: Calculate availability, workload, projections and recommendations within the agency.
public.privacy.section2.item3: Provide support, answer inquiries and maintain the operational continuity of the service.
public.privacy.section2.item4: Prevent unauthorized access, investigate incidents and preserve traceability of relevant events.
public.privacy.section2.item5: Improve the platform using aggregated or de-identified information, where appropriate.
public.privacy.section3.title: 3. Access and separation between agencies
public.privacy.section3.paragraph1: TeamBalance is designed with an agency-isolation approach. Each operation must be associated with the authenticated organization and the applicable role permissions in order to prevent one agency from accessing another’s information.
public.privacy.section3.paragraph2: Within the same agency, the administrator must determine who can access data about projects, people, costs or other operational indicators.
public.privacy.section4.title: 4. Information retention
public.privacy.section4.paragraph1: Information is retained for the time needed to operate the account, provide support, preserve traceability and comply with applicable obligations. Specific periods may vary according to the type of data, subscription status, backup needs and current regulations.
public.privacy.section4.paragraph2: The planned functional architecture includes audit records, backups and archiving mechanisms for operational information. These controls are intended to enable recovery after incidents and avoid retaining information longer than necessary.
public.privacy.section5.title: 5. Rights of data subjects
public.privacy.section5.paragraph1: Data subjects may request information about their data and, where applicable, request access, updating, correction or deletion. When data is entered by a customer agency, the request should first be directed through the organization that manages that account.
public.privacy.section5.paragraph2: TeamBalance must provide a contact channel for these requests and handle them in accordance with applicable personal-data protection law.
public.privacy.section6.title: 6. Changes to this policy
public.privacy.section6.paragraph1: This policy may be updated when features, processing practices or applicable obligations change. The current version will remain available on this site together with its update date.
public.privacy.notice: TeamBalance keeps this policy available so customer organizations can understand how information is processed within the service.
public.security.title: Protecting information is part of the product.
public.security.lead: TeamBalance is designed to manage agency operational information with access controls, traceability and continuity.
public.security.section1.title: 1. Role-based access
public.security.section1.paragraph1: The platform supports role-based authorization to differentiate the actions and information available to Owners, Project Managers and Employees. Sensitive data, such as costs and profitability indicators, must remain restricted to authorized profiles.
public.security.section1.paragraph2: Accounts use individual credentials and time-limited sessions. The architecture includes access-recovery mechanisms and login-attempt logging to help identify unusual activity.
public.security.section2.title: 2. Data and communications protection
public.security.section2.paragraph1: TeamBalance is designed to encrypt communications between the browser and server through secure protocols, together with protection mechanisms for stored operational and personal data. Passwords must not be stored or transmitted as plain text.
public.security.section2.paragraph2: Each agency’s information is handled separately through identifiers and validations applicable to each operation, reducing the risk of cross-organization access.
public.security.section3.title: 3. Audit and traceability
public.security.section3.paragraph1: Relevant actions involving projects, assignments, status changes and access may be recorded in an activity log. This traceability supports operational monitoring, incident investigation and review of activities that require oversight.
public.security.section3.paragraph2: Authentication and security events are considered part of audit records, following the principles of necessity, restricted access and limited retention.
public.security.section4.title: 4. Continuity and backups
public.security.section4.paragraph1: The planned architecture includes basic availability monitoring, backups and recovery procedures for failures. These mechanisms seek to protect service continuity and allow information to be restored after technical incidents.
public.security.section4.paragraph2: Security and availability require ongoing review. Controls may evolve alongside infrastructure, identified risks and customer-organization needs.
public.security.section5.title: 5. Shared responsibility for security
public.security.section5.paragraph1: Security also depends on the practices of each agency. Administrators must assign the minimum permissions needed, keep authorized users up to date and report any suspicious access or incident that could affect the account.
public.security.notice: Security is reviewed continuously to support the evolution of the platform, infrastructure and the needs of customer organizations.
